This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 & 227 Of Constitu Tion Of India Praying To Quash The Order Passed By The Respondent No.1 In No.Rb/Ns/Fssa/Cr-01/2016-17 Dated 25.03.2017, Produced A T Annexu Re-E, Etc.,. This Writ Petition Coming On For Orders, This Day, The Court Made The Fo Llowing : Order
texts.facts: On the earlier date of hearing, the learned Addl. Government Advocate submitted that an alternative efficacious remedy is available by way of an appeal before the tribunal under Section 76 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, but this day she fairly submits on the instructions given by the 1 s t respondent, before this Court, that no tribunal yet has been constituted by the State. The brief factual matrix of the case is that the petitioner is a small scale businessman who obtained proper authorization or licence from the Government for the purpose of starting a pure drinking water unit in Belagavi. Accordingly he has started running the business. That on 19.9.2016 the respondent No.2 has visited the working unit of the petitioner. At that time the petitioner was not present. However the 3rd respondent was present at that time and it is alleged that the petitioner has been running the said unit without ISI certificate and also running the same without proper licence. The respondent No.2 found, 37 packed water cans and 3 empty water cans in the said unit and he has seized them for the purpose of sending the same for scientific examination to the laboratory. Accordingly the case has been registered against the petitioner in No.RB/NS/FSSA/CR-01/ 2016-17. The Additional Deputy Commissioner and the Authorized Officer under the Food and Civil Supplies Act, has conducted the enquiry and passed the impugned order as Premanand S/O Ganapati Kavale vs The Ex-Officio & Additional on 14 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165701703/ 2 per Annexure-E imposing penalty of `2,00,000/- on the petitioner directing him to pay the said amount within one month and also directed not to indulge in manufacturing misbranded articles and also directed him to destroy the misbranded articles in his unit.
texts.arguments: 4. The learned counsel for the petitioner drawn attention of this Court that a notice was issued to the petitioner to appear before the respondent No.1 on 10.1.2017 at 11.30 a.m. and subsequently the case has been adjourned and on 7.2.2017 the case was taken up and on that day after hearing both the parties the order has been passed on the same day imposing penalty. The learned counsel seriously contends that no opportunity has been given to the petitioner to file his objections or to lead any evidence nor the evidence of the said Sri M.S.Bekkeri who has not been subjected to any cross examination.

The learned counsel seriously contends that no opportunity has been given to the petitioner to file his objections or to lead any evidence nor the evidence of the said Sri M.S.Bekkeri who has not been subjected to any cross examination.
